description.narrative: The funding to WATHI in West and Central Africa is core support the implementation of WATHI’s mandate in working to advance citizen engagement to accelerate political, social and cultural change and human development in West Africa in 2026. In line with the approach of WATHI which calls both for an in-depth understanding of local contexts and expectations and the need to learn from experiences from countries around the world, WATHI proposes to stimulate expand the scope of the partnership to also focus on gender equality and rights, in addition to their continued work on supporting the West African public debate on education and training. This year the programme will include a three-day in-person training workshop for 25 participants on increasing youth capacity linked to equality and women's rights, with three key dimensions: the international and regional framework on women's rights, advocacy, and the use of social media to raise awareness about women's rights and the threats girls face online.
